image_description: The image displays two Nile crocodiles in a semi-aquatic enclosure. The primary subject is a large adult crocodile positioned in the center-right, basking on a grassy bank with its mouth wide open (gaping), revealing the interior of the jaw and teeth. A second, smaller juvenile crocodile is visible in the bottom-left foreground, resting on a concrete ledge near the water. The background consists of dense green foliage and trees.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The main subject's head profile is clearly visible; the snout tapers to a V-shape consistent with Crocodylus niloticus morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of osteoderms are visible along the spine and back of the main subject.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs of the main subject are largely obscured by the body angle and vegetation. The digit count cannot be verified visually.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending into the background, appearing muscular and consistent with crocodilian anatomy.
